prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There isn’t a single universally “best” roofing company for hurricane-rated replacements in Miami — the best choice depends on the product you want (shingles, metal, tile), your budget, and which contractor has the right certifications, local experience and references. That said, you should only hire a contractor who knows and complies with Miami‑Dade/HVHZ requirements and who is factory‑certified for the system you choose.

How to find the best contractor (quick checklist)
- Verify licensing and insurance
  - Check the contractor’s Florida license and status on the Florida DBPR website.
  - Confirm general liability and workers’ compensation insurance and get certificates naming you as additional insured during the job.
- Verify hurricane‑rated product and installation approvals
  - Ensure materials are Miami‑Dade County Product Approved (NOA) or otherwise meet FBC/HVHZ requirements.
  - Insist the contractor is a factory‑certified installer for the manufacturer (GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Preferred, etc.) for warranty validity.
- Ask for written warranties
  - Get the manufacturer’s warranty in writing AND a separate workmanship warranty from the contractor (length and details).
- Check experience and references
  - 5+ years doing hurricane-rated roofs in Miami/Dade County, with recent local references and photos of finished projects.
  - Check reviews (Google, BBB, Angi/Yelp) and ask for at least 3 references you can call.
- Permits, inspection and lien releases
  - Contractor must pull permits and schedule inspections. Get a final lien release and proof of permit closeout.
- Get multiple bids and compare scope
  - At least 2–3 written estimates that list materials, underlayment, fasteners, flashing, ventilation, tie-ins, roof deck repairs, and warranty details.
- Red flags
  - Pressure to sign immediately, demands for large upfront cash, no permit pull, vague warranty language, or untraceable company address.

What to ask every contractor (short script)
- “Are you licensed in Florida? What is your license number?”
- “Are you certified by the manufacturer for this product? Can you provide the certification?”
- “Will you use materials with Miami‑Dade NOA/HVHZ approval? Can I see the NOA?”
- “Who will pull the permits and handle inspections?”
- “What is included in your workmanship warranty? Length?”
- “Can you provide 3 local references and photos of finished hurricane-rated jobs?”

Product and system considerations for hurricane zones
- Metal and interlocking tile/metal standing seam often perform better in high winds than typical 3‑tab shingles; properly installed architectural shingles with approved attachment systems can also meet HVHZ requirements.
- Pay attention to attachment methods (screws/fasteners, adhesive/tape systems, specialized clips) and to details like eave/soffit reinforcement, wind‑rated underlayment, and secondary water barriers.
- Ventilation and deck fastening/methods can be as important as the roof covering for wind performance.

How I can help
- If you give your Miami ZIP code or a few contractor names you’ve been quoted by, I can help you evaluate them (what to probe, what to look for in their paperwork).
- If you want, I can provide a short email or call script to use when contacting contractors.

If you’d like, tell me your ZIP code and the roof material you prefer (shingle, metal, tile) and I’ll suggest ways to locate highly rated certified installers in your immediate area.
